items.title: A Framework for Finished Goods Safety Stock Estimation Using Local LLM-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
items.abstract: This study proposes a local LLM-RAG-based framework for estimating finished-goods safety stock in high-mix low-volume manufacturing environments. The proposed framework maintains a statistical safety stock calculation as a quantitative anchor and complements it with context-aware reasoning using a local Large Language Model (LLM) and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). The framework first preprocesses ERP/MES data through SQL-based filtering and calculates dynamic indicators such as risk lead time, seasonality, urgent-order volatility, demand trends, and open orders. These indicators are then injected into the local LLM as structured RAG context to generate explainable safety stock adjustment rationales. The framework was implemented using empirical data from an automotive parts supplier and applied to 180 finished-goods items. The developed program generated safety stock output logs over 22 ASOF points from January to May 2026. Because safety stock is a policy-level reference value linked to production planning and MRP, the quantitative evaluation was conducted using five monthly closing points. The results showed positive penalty improvement in all monthly closing periods, while the delivery response proxy increased from 80.7% to 83.0%. These findings indicate that the proposed framework can support context-aware safety stock adjustment by jointly considering ABC grade, seasonality, demand trends, urgent-order volatility, and open orders, while avoiding excessive weekly fluctuations in policy-level safety stock values.

items.title: A Large-Scale Simulated Dataset for Potato Crop with AI-Relevant Challenges
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly influential in modeling and optimizing complex agricultural systems. However, publicly available large-scale agricultural datasets that present unique and significant AI challenges remain limited. In this paper, we introduce an extensive simulated dataset for potato crop production targeting Florida-like off-season growing conditions: a setting characterized by sandy soils, limited nutrient retention, and heightened sensitivity to weather and management variability. This dataset is generated using the DSSAT (Decision Support System for Agrotechnology Transfer) modeling framework and its Potato module. A key contribution of this work is the careful calibration of DSSAT parameters against real ground truth observations, a process that is well known to be non-trivial and time consuming, with no single standardized protocol typically requiring iterative trial-and-error adjustment of crop-specific genetic coefficients.This dataset provides a reproducible, agronomically calibrated starting point for researchers to build upon directly. The dataset comprises approximately 4.9 million crop-management scenarios varying planting dates, fertilizer rates, irrigation strategies, and historical weather yielding over 675 million daily data points across 24 years. Beyond its agricultural scope, this dataset presents a range of AI-specific challenges, including multivariate time-series forecasting, rare-event prediction, and early forecasting, making it a valuable benchmark for the broader machine learning and time-series research communities.

items.title: A multimodal framework for UAV-assisted wildfire detection and contextual alert generation using vision-language models and LLM fusion
items.abstract: The increasing frequency and intensity of wildfires pose a critical threat to ecosystems, property, and human life, creating a need for monitoring systems that combine rapid visual detection with interpretable and actionable reporting. This study presents an integrated multimodal framework for UAV-assisted wildfire monitoring that combines YOLOv12n-based wildfire and smoke detection, Moondream2-based vision-language captioning, and GPT-4o mini-based alert summarization. YOLOv12n is evaluated against six YOLO baselines on an aerial wildfire and smoke dataset and achieves a favorable balance between detection performance and computational efficiency, with an overall precision of 0.649, recall of 0.628, mAP@0.5 of 0.628, an inference time of 1.8 ms, and a model size of 2.52 million parameters. For semantic scene understanding, Moondream2 achieves the highest average BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, and METEOR scores among the evaluated vision-language models. GPT-4o mini similarly outperforms the evaluated summarization baselines in summary-reference alignment, achieving average BLEU-4, ROUGE-L, and METEOR scores of 0.1501, 0.5595, and 0.5461, respectively. Qualitative analysis across five wildfire video scenarios further illustrates the pipeline’s ability to generate contextually relevant descriptions and concise draft alerts under varied visual conditions. Computational measurements for the locally executed models were obtained on a backend workstation, whereas GPT-4o mini was accessed through an external API; therefore, embedded UAV performance and network-inclusive end-to-end latency remain to be validated. Overall, the results demonstrate the potential of combining lightweight visual detection, vision-language reasoning, and LLM-based summarization to support human-verified wildfire situational awareness and emergency decision-making.

items.title: A note on data-efficient finetuning of vision foundation models
items.abstract: Adapting foundation models to a new task within or beyond the training domain is the de facto standard for building specialized machine learning models. Recently, Visual Prompting (VP) has emerged as a promising technique for efficient knowledge transfer. As new foundation model families~(like Mamba) get introduced and VP pipelines such as AutoVP reach greater maturity, we find a growing need for a systematic evaluation of current approaches. In this work, we assess the performance of the latest models, comparing them to earlier architectures and alternative fine-tuning methods, to better understand the progress, challenges and opportunities in the field of efficient fine-tuning under resource limitations. Towards this goal, this paper provides a concise empirical overview of the interactions among foundation model families (Attention-, Convolution-, and Mamba-based) and transfer paradigms: VP, Linear Probing (LP), Full Fine-tuning (FFT) and Low Rank Adaptation (LoRA). Our work builds up on previous findings by broadening the selection of evaluated models and techniques while tuning hyperparameters. In the interest of delivering practical guidelines for the user, we also explore application of prevalent regularization techniques to boost performance in the context of VP.
